'''''Zanthoxylum simulans''''', the '''Chinese-pepper''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=ZASI2|taxon=Zanthoxylum simulans|access-date=9 August 2015}}</ref> '''Chinese prickly-ash''' or '''flatspine prickly-ash''', is a [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Rutaceae]], native to southern and central [[China]], [[Taiwan]], and South Korea.<ref name = powo/> It is one of several species of ''[[Zanthoxylum]]'' from which [[Sichuan pepper]] is produced.

It is a spreading [[shrub]] or small [[tree]] growing to 7 m tall. The [[leaf|leaves]] are 7–12.5 cm long, pinnate, with 7–11 leaflets, the leaflets 3–5 cm long and 1.5–2 cm broad. There are numerous short (3–6 mm) spines on both the stems and the leaf petioles, and large (several cm) knobs on the branches. The [[flower]]s are produced in slender [[inflorescence|cyme]]s, each flower about 4–5 mm diameter. The 3–4 mm berry has a rough reddish brown shell that splits open to release the black seeds from inside.
[[File:Zanthoxylum simulans kz1.JPG|thumb|left|Leaves and fruit]]

==Subspecies==
Two subspecies are accepted.<ref name = powo/>
*''Zanthoxylum simulans'' subsp. ''calcareum'' {{small|Z.H.Chen, Feng Chen & W.Zhu}} – Zhejiang
*''Zanthoxylum simulans'' subsp. ''simulans'' – central and southern China, South Korea, and Taiwan
